question: Cherry-pink post-mortem lividity (livor mortis) is a pathognomonic finding for carbon monoxide poisoning.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This statement is true. Cherry-pink lividity is caused by carboxyhaemoglobin (HbCO), which is bright red (unlike the purple-blue of deoxyhaemoglobin). It is a key post-mortem indicator of CO poisoning alongside cherry-red organs at autopsy.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. Cherry-pink lividity results from the bright red carboxyhaemoglobin (HbCO) complex, which persists post-mortem and imparts the characteristic colour to skin, mucosae, and internal organs including the brain.
